headline: Mostly sunny, dry and milder than normal through Saturday; a coastal storm could then bring 1–2 inches of rain or more and gusty winds late Sunday into Monday, but whether it comes close enough is still very uncertain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Strong high pressure keeps New York City and the surrounding area mostly sunny and dry through Wednesday evening, with no watches or advisories in effect. Winds stay light, about 6–9 mph from the northwest to west-southwest late this afternoon, then drop to around 5 mph or less tonight and go calm in many areas outside the city. With clear skies and calm air, how cold it gets overnight will depend mainly on how quickly the ground loses heat, so outlying spots will run cooler than the city and coast.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday through Saturday stay mostly sunny and dry under the same high pressure, with highs several degrees above normal, in the upper 50s to mid 60s. Winds stay light on Thursday, around 3–9 mph. Nights remain clear and calm, but overnight lows will gradually ease to a few to several degrees above normal late in the week and into the weekend, especially in the city and right along the coast.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A storm is likely to form off the Southeast coast this weekend and then head northeast as a dip in the jet stream approaches. If it tracks close enough, rain and wind would spread up the coast late Sunday and continue through Monday, possibly tapering Monday afternoon, with 1–2 inches of rain possible and locally more, plus gusts of 30–40 mph in parts of the area; the chance of rain is currently 30–60%. The American model and its AI version show this closer track, while the European model is slower and keeps the storm farther south and east—stronger, but far enough offshore to have limited impact—and rain totals could drop off sharply on the storm's western edge.

coast: Calm boating conditions through Sunday morning with no advisories: winds mostly from the northwest to west under 15 knots (about 17 mph) and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 feet. Small Craft Advisory conditions are possible later Sunday into Monday, depending on the track and strength of the coastal storm.
watch_for: Whether the late Sunday–Monday storm tracks close to the coast (1–2+ inches of rain and 30–40 mph gusts) or stays offshore and mostly misses.
Where the sharp western edge of the rain sets up, which could mean big differences in totals over short distances.
confidence: High confidence in dry, mild weather through Saturday; low confidence in the track, timing and rain totals for the late Sunday–Monday storm.
